baselineSpikesPerSec.note: Round resting rate in the mammalian canal-afferent range. Not copied from a checked table. Goldberg JM, Fernandez C. J Neurophysiol. 1971;34(4):635-660 is the usual squirrel-monkey paper; the 90 was not read off that page.

afferentGainSpikesPerDegPerSec.note: Chosen so a constant-rate afferent reaches the inhibitory floor near 180 deg/s (baseline divided by this gain). Not copied from a checked table.

cupulaTimeConstantSec.source: Raphan T. Vestibular, locomotor, and vestibulo-autonomic research: 50 years of collaboration with Bernard Cohen. J Neurophysiol. 123(1):329-345. doi:10.1152/jn.00485.2019. That review says the human cupular time constant is about 4 s (Dai et al. 1999) and the monkey afferent time constant is about 3.5–5 s (Goldberg and Fernandez 1971). The 4 s figure is taken from that sentence.
cupulaTimeConstantSec.note: Dominant cupula (long) time constant. The short mechanical time constant is not modelled.

velocityStorageSec.source: Raphan T, Matsuo V, Cohen B. Velocity storage in the vestibulo-ocular reflex arc (VOR). Exp Brain Res. 1979;35:229-248. Cited for the mechanism. The 16 s value was not copied from a table in that paper.
velocityStorageSec.note: Round teaching value for a central time constant longer than the cupula. Unverified.

vorGain.note: Ideal compensatory gain for this teaching model, so a full canal pair can oppose head velocity. Not a measured human constant.

plantScale.note: Agonist contraction and antagonist relaxation each carry the canal axis, so 0.5 keeps the pair from adding twice. Model coefficient, not a measured constant.

fastPhaseThresholdDeg.note: Eye-position magnitude that starts a reset toward the centre. The fast phase is this reset, so nystagmus is not scripted as a separate animation.

fastPhaseSpeedDegPerSec.note: Reset speed while the eye is past the threshold. Not copied from a checked table.

fastPhaseStopDeg.note: The reset ends inside this distance of the centre, or as soon as it would cross the centre.
